LMP3.title: Graff end United's winning run on Tockwith's pole day
LMP3.dek: Trouillet, Petit and Guibbert won in Graff's #9 Ligier, about five seconds clear of Duqueine's #19, with championship leaders United third and pole-sitting debutants Tockwith sixth after a late spin.

chapters.title: A 20-car class and a new name on the sheet
text: United Autosports arrived at Paul Ricard as the LMP3 championship leader, with the #2 Ligier of Brundle, Guasch and England having won the three rounds so far. The class had grown to 20 cars, and the biggest newcomer was Tockwith Motorsports, the Yorkshire team stepping up from the Michelin GT3 Le Mans Cup, where it had run an Audi R8 LMS. Moore and Hanson, who share the #26 Ligier, had been on track at Wednesday's test and said they were pleased with their apparent pace.

Elsewhere there was little change. Graff ran its third chassis, an older car that now carried the #10 for Falb, Rayhall and Potolicchio, and By Speed Factory's #5 had Hartshorne back aboard. The four-hour race was set for two long pit stops rather than the usual three, each with a reference time of 1m45s. Tockwith topped Friday's first practice with Moore's 1:54.6 ahead of Sernagiotto's Villorba Corse #7 and Gachet's Panis Barthez #16; on Saturday morning Brundle led for United on 1:54.869, with Kaiser's 360 Racing #6 and the #18 Yvan Muller-run car behind. United's second car, the #3, needed an engine change after that session.

chapters.title: Moore takes pole by nearly eight tenths
text: Moore put the debutant Tockwith Ligier on pole with a 1:54.006, 0.790 seconds clear of Guibbert in Graff's #9 and 0.811 ahead of Gachet's Panis Barthez #16, which was only two hundredths behind the Graff. Brundle was fourth for United on 1:55.238 and Kaiser fifth for 360 Racing, with the next several cars separated by only a few hundredths.

The #3 United Ligier of Patterson, Bell and Boyd did not set a time after its engine problem and started from the back of the field, 39th overall. Cougnaud's #18 was sixth and Rayhall's second Graff, the #10, seventh, while Oak's #4 qualified slowest of the timed cars, 4.4 seconds off pole.

chapters.title: Moore leads, United lose places
text: Moore stayed in control of the first stint ahead of Guibbert, while Brundle, who had taken Gachet on the opening lap, soon lost ground to Mondini's Eurointernational #11 and Rayhall's #10; the United driver reported a lack of straight-line speed on the long Mistral straight. Gachet was also passed by the pair. After the first stops Trouillet led for Graff, but Mondini briefly got ahead of him, with Sernagiotto third for Villorba Corse.

chapters.title: Strategy reshuffles the order
text: The cars yo-yoed through the order as each took its two long stops at different moments. At the midpoint Trouillet was back in front in the #9 after a slow stop had dropped Hanson to fourth in the Tockwith car. A full-course yellow to recover the stranded RLR MSport Ligier, the #15, came around half-distance, and the order after the second round of stops had Trouillet still ahead, Moore back in the #26, Heriau third in Ultimate's #17, then Hallyday in the Duqueine #19 and England in the #2 United.

Moore took the lead on track with just under an hour and twenty minutes left, while Hallyday passed Heriau for third and England then caught and passed both Heriau and Hallyday. Guasch had taken over the #2 after about an hour and kept it in touch with the #19 despite the car's straight-line deficit.

chapters.title: Hanson spins, Lunardi holds off England
text: Moore stopped and Hanson rejoined second, behind the #9, which Petit now drove. Then, at the final corner of a lap, Hanson spun, and the Tockwith car dropped out of the podium fight, eventually finishing sixth. Lunardi in the #19 moved up to second, with England closing in the United, but the Duqueine driver pulled out a gap of nearly 30 seconds in the final stint. Petit crossed the line around five seconds ahead of Lunardi to give Graff the win, with England third.

chapters.title: First defeat for United
text: Trouillet, Petit and Guibbert took the #9 Graff to the class win on 117 laps, with David Hallyday, Droux and Lunardi second in the #19 and Brundle, Guasch and England third in the #2, all on the same lap. It was the first class defeat of the season for United, whose car remained at the top of the standings. Ultimate's #17 and 360 Racing's #6 were next on 116 laps, ahead of Tockwith's #26, which also set the class fastest lap, a 1:55.151. Inter Europol's #13 was seventh.

United's second car, the #3, was three laps behind the class winners. Graff's #10, Eurointernational's #11, RACE Performance's #8, RLR's #15 and the #18 were not classified. The series next goes to Spa-Francorchamps on 25 September.

facts.v: Graff became the first LMP3 team to beat United Autosports to a class win this season, after the Leeds team had won every round before Paul Ricard.

LMGTE.title: JMW use the yellow to take a second win
LMGTE.dek: Smith, Butcher and Bertolini won in JMW's Ferrari #66 after pitting under a full-course yellow, finishing ahead of Formula Racing's Ferrari while pole-sitting Aston Martin took third.

chapters.title: Eight cars and a BoP adjustment
text: Eight GTE cars entered the Paul Ricard round, Ferrari 458s from four teams, two Proton Porsches and one Aston Martin. The class had been shared out so far: Aston Martin Racing was promoted to the Silverstone win when JMW's car was excluded, Proton won at Imola and JMW's #66 took the Red Bull Ring. For this race the Ferraris gained 5kg to 1,240kg, while the Porsche 911 and Aston Martin V8 Vantage stayed at 1,205kg and 1,230kg. All three models lost 5 litres of fuel capacity, leaving the Porsche on 90, the Ferrari on 85 and the Aston on 95.

There were three driver changes. Pier Guidi was back in AT Racing's #56 after another driver had been announced, Jensen replaced Christina Nielsen in Formula Racing's #60 and David Jahn made his GTE debut in Proton's #88. Pier Guidi topped Friday's first practice with a 1:58.080, just 0.027 ahead of Turner's Aston, and Cioci's AF Corse #51 led on Saturday morning with 1:57.406.

chapters.title: Turner breaks the Ferrari grip
text: Turner interrupted the Ferrari run of practice by putting Aston Martin Racing's #99 on pole with a 1:56.285. Pier Guidi was 0.198 behind in the AT Racing Ferrari, with Griffin third in AF Corse's #55 and Bertolini fourth for JMW's #66. Seven of the eight cars were covered by a little over a second: Cioci in the AF Corse #51 and Mac in Formula Racing's #60 both set 1:57.2s, and Henzler's Proton Porsche #77 was seventh on 1:57.325.
The sister Proton, the #88, never set a time because of a technical problem and started from the back of the grid.

chapters.title: Howard drops, Butcher takes the lead
text: Howard lost four places for Aston Martin on the first lap after starting from pole. After about 20 minutes Butcher took the lead from Scott's #55 with a move on the inside into Signes, having had the better exit onto the Mistral straight. Talkanitsa Jr and Laursen ran third and fourth for AT Racing and Formula Racing, ahead of Howard. At the first stops Smith took over the #66 and kept the lead.

chapters.title: The yellows decide it
text: A full-course yellow to recover the stranded RLR MSport LMP3 Ligier proved the key. Smith pitted under it, and Bertolini took over with an advantage of more than 30 seconds. A second yellow, after Cameron's AF Corse Ferrari was spun at the pit entrance by a Graff LMP3 car, gave Jensen a similar boost for Formula Racing, while Cameron lost time and had to restart. Turner ran third for Aston Martin, with the Talkanitsas' AT Racing car, which had not pitted under the yellows, fourth.
Butcher got back into the JMW car with just over an hour to go, second behind an out-of-sequence Turner until the Aston made its stop.

chapters.title: Fuel scare, no change of order
text: The finish looked uneventful until the JMW and Formula Racing Ferraris both needed splash-and-dash fuel stops in the final 10 minutes. It changed nothing. MacDowall was too far back in the Aston to profit and took third ahead of Pier Guidi in the AT Racing Ferrari, while Griffin brought the AF Corse #55 home fifth.

chapters.title: JMW take a second win
text: Smith, Butcher and Bertolini won in JMW's #66 on 115 laps. Laursen, Mac and Jensen were second for Formula Racing in the #60, Howard, Turner and MacDowall third in the pole-sitting Aston Martin #99 and the Talkanitsas with Pier Guidi fourth in AT Racing's #56. AF Corse's #55 (Cameron, Griffin, Scott) was fifth and Proton's #77 sixth, all six classified cars on the same lap. Pier Guidi set the class fastest lap, a 1:58.676.

It was a second win of the season for JMW, which had been excluded from its Silverstone result. AF Corse's #51 and Proton's #88 were not classified. The series next goes to Spa-Francorchamps on 25 September.

facts.v: Ferrari weight rose 5kg to 1,240kg and every GTE car lost 5 litres of tank capacity, leaving the Porsche on 90 litres, Ferrari on 85 and Aston Martin on 95.
Turner's 1:56.285 put the Aston Martin #99 ahead of Pier Guidi's AT Racing Ferrari and broke the Ferrari grip on practice.

facts.v: JMW Motorsport became the first repeat GTE winners of the season, with Butcher, Bertolini and Smith.
